evidence_items.publisher: Barnett and colleagues, Deakin University; arXiv
evidence_items.explanation: Three engineering case studies identify unresolved retrieval and generation failures, including failure despite the answer being supplied in context. The January report documents the then-existing reliability limitations; individual test days are not specified.

The contemporary survey credits RAG with meaningful benefits. This limits any interpretation of 'infancy' as uselessness, while remaining consistent with Marcus's acknowledgment of strong results on some tasks.

unresolved_gaps: No finite literature search can prove the literal absence of every possible correctness result.
The evidence supports unresolved reliability problems, not an objective developmental age or a conclusion that no RAG application was production-ready.
